explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result, and I don't expect one: every object in the statement is defined in the library itself. These are `ideleSumLocalInv`, `ideleLocalInvAt`, `ideleInfiniteInvAt`, `ideleSupport`, `ideleFormation`, `NormalLayer` and `L.H`, the class-field-theory and continuous-cohomology setup built in TauCeti. Mathlib has no idele class formation and no local invariant maps, so it cannot hold this formula. The formula says the sum of local invariants equals the finite sum over any finite set S of places containing the support, plus the sum over the infinite places. The proof uses only the library's own lemmas (`sumLocalInv_eq_sum`, `ideleLocalInvAt_eq_zero_of_notMem_ideleSupport`, and the `_apply` simp lemmas), so the mathematical content lies in the library's definitions. I identified this from the statement and proof alone and did not run any searches in the Mathlib sources.
